akhfash:4-4.t: The place of its oath — and Allah knows best — is upon ﴿قُتِلَ أَصْحَابُ ٱلأُخْدُودِ﴾; He left the lām implied, as He said ﴿وَٱلشَّمْسِ وَضُحَاهَا﴾ … ﴿قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن زَكَّاهَا﴾, meaning, if Allah wills, "لَقَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ زَكَّاهَا" ("he has surely succeeded who purifies it"), and dropped the lām. And if you wish, (it is) by way of putting forward (taqdīm), as if He said ﴿قُتِلَ أَصْحَابُ ٱلأُخْدُودِ﴾ ﴿وَٱلسَّمَآءِ ذَاتِ ٱلْبُرُوجِ﴾ [1]. And some said (the oath is upon) ﴿إِنَّ بَطْشَ رَبِّكَ لَشَدِيدٌ﴾.

akhfash:5-5.t:
As for His words ﴿ٱلنَّارِ ذَاتِ ٱلْوَقُودِ﴾, it is a badal (substitute).
As for ﴿ٱلْوَقُودِ﴾, it is the firewood, and "الوُقُودُ" (with ḍamma) is the act, which is "الاتِّقاد" (burning).

akhfash:15-15.t: And He said ﴿ذُو ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱلْمَجِيد﴾: ﴿ٱلْمَجِيد﴾ is genitive following ﴿ٱلْعَرْشِ﴾, and nominative following His word ﴿ذُو﴾. Likewise ﴿مَّحْفُوظ﴾ is genitive following "اللَّوْح" (the Tablet) and nominative following "القرآن" (the Qur'an).

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿وَالسَّمَاءِ ذَاتِ الْبُرُوجِ﴾: the stars — twelve constellations, which were mentioned previously in [Sūrat] al-Furqān.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَشَاهِدٍ﴾: Friday, ﴿وَمَشْهُودٍ﴾: the Day of ʿArafa. Thus the three were explained in the hadith: the first is promised; the second is a witness to the deeds done in it; and the third is witnessed by the people and the angels. The answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam) has its beginning omitted; its implied form is «لقد» ("Indeed, …").

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿قُتِلَ﴾: cursed are ﴿أَصْحَابُ الْأُخْدُودِ﴾: the trench in the ground.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿النَّارِ﴾: a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from it. ﴿ذَاتِ الْوَقُودِ﴾: that with which it is kindled.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿إِذْ هُمْ عَلَيْهَا﴾, that is, around it, at the edge of the trench, on chairs, ﴿قُعُودٌ﴾

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَهُمْ عَلَى مَا يَفْعَلُونَ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ in Allah — tormenting them by throwing them into the fire if they did not turn back from their faith — ﴿شُهُودٌ﴾: present. It is narrated that Allah saved the believers who were thrown into the fire by taking their souls before they fell into it, and the fire came out upon those who were there and burned them.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَمَا نَقَمُوا مِنْهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ﴾ in His dominion, ﴿الْحَمِيدِ﴾: the Praised,

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿الَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ﴾, that is, the disbelievers objected to nothing in the believers except their faith.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ فَتَنُوا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ﴾ by burning ﴿ثُمَّ لَمْ يَتُوبُوا فَلَهُمْ عَذَابُ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ for their disbelief ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَذَابُ الْحَرِيقِ﴾, that is, the punishment for their burning of the believers, in the Hereafter. It is also said: in this world, in that the fire came out and burned them, as mentioned previously.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ ذَلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْكَبِيرُ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿إِنَّ بَطْشَ رَبِّكَ﴾ against the disbelievers ﴿لَشَدِيدٌ﴾ in accordance with His will.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ هُوَ يُبْدِئُ﴾ creation ﴿وَيُعِيدُ﴾, so nothing He wills is beyond Him.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ﴾ to the sinning believers, ﴿الْوَدُودُ﴾: showing love to His friends by honouring them.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿ذُو الْعَرْشِ﴾: its Creator and Owner, ﴿الْمَجِيدُ﴾ — with the nominative (rafʿ) — the One deserving of the perfection of the attributes of highness.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿فَعَّالٌ لِمَا يُرِيدُ﴾: nothing is beyond Him.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿فِرْعَوْنَ وَثَمُودَ﴾: a badal (substitute) from «الجنود»; mentioning Pharaoh suffices for mentioning his followers. Their story is that they were destroyed for their disbelief. This is a warning to those who disbelieve in the Prophet ﷺ and the Qur'an, so that they take heed.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿بَلِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فِي تَكْذِيبٍ﴾ of what has been mentioned.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ مِنْ وَرَائِهِمْ مُحِيطٌ﴾: there is no protector for them from Him.

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿فِي لَوْحٍ﴾ — it is in the air above the seventh heaven — ﴿مَحْفُوظٍ﴾ — with the genitive (jarr) — from the devils and from any part of it being altered. Its length is what lies between the heaven and the earth, its breadth what lies between the east and the west, and it is made of a white pearl. Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said this.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿وَالسَّماءِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "أقسم" (I swear); ﴿ذاتِ الْبُرُوجِ﴾: naʿt (adjective), muḍāf to البروج; and البروج are the stars in the sky.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿وَالْيَوْمِ﴾: conjoined to السماء; ﴿الْمَوْعُودِ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of اليوم.

daas-irab:3-3.t: Both conjoined to what precedes them.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿قُتِلَ﴾: a passive past verb; ﴿أَصْحابُ الْأُخْدُودِ﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), muḍāf to الأخدود; the verbal clause is the answer to the oath.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿النَّارِ﴾: a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl, a substitute) for أصحاب الأخدود; ﴿ذاتِ الْوَقُودِ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of النار, muḍāf to الوقود.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿إِذْ هُمْ﴾: an adverb of time and a mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿عَلَيْها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); ﴿قُعُودٌ﴾: khabar; the nominal clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿وَهُمْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and ﴿هُمْ﴾ is mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿عَلى ما﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) شهود; ﴿يَفْعَلُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: attached to the verb; ﴿شُهُودٌ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle and ﴿ما﴾ is negative; ﴿نَقَمُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of exception; ﴿أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, the wāw being its agent; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾: attached to the verb; ﴿الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ﴾: two badals (substitutes) for the Name of Majesty.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a third badal (substitute) for the Name of Majesty; ﴿لَهُ﴾: fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿مُلْكُ﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾: conjoined to السموات. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾: mubtadaʾ; ﴿عَلى كُلِّ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar شهيد; ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿شَهِيدٌ﴾: khabar.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿فَتَنُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ﴾: conjoined to المؤمنين; the verbal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿لَمْ يَتُوبُوا﴾: an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, the wāw being its agent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَلَهُمْ﴾: the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); ﴿لَهُمْ عَذابُ﴾: fronted khabar (predicate) and postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿جَهَنَّمَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the nominal clause is the khabar of inna, and the clause إن الذين… is resumptive. ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَذابُ الْحَرِيقِ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿آمَنُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين; ﴿وَعَمِلُوا﴾: conjoined to آمنوا; ﴿الصَّالِحاتِ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٌ﴾: fronted khabar (predicate) and postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is the khabar of inna, and the clause إن الذين… is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿تَجْرِي﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ); ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿الْأَنْهارُ﴾: agent; the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of جنات. ﴿ذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ﴾: mubtadaʾ and its khabar; ﴿الْكَبِيرُ﴾: adjective; the nominal clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿إِنَّ بَطْشَ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿لَشَدِيدٌ﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and ﴿شديد﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of inna; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿هُوَ﴾: a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); ﴿يُبْدِئُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the clause إنه gives the reason (taʿlīl); ﴿وَيُعِيدُ﴾: conjoined to يبدئ.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الْوَدُودُ﴾: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and two predicates (khabar); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿ذُو الْعَرْشِ﴾: ذو is a third khabar (predicate), muḍāf to العرش; ﴿الْمَجِيدُ﴾: also a khabar.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿فَعَّالٌ﴾: also a khabar (predicate); ﴿لِما﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them; ﴿يُرِيدُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿هَلْ﴾: an interrogative particle; ﴿أَتاكَ﴾: a past verb and its object; ﴿حَدِيثُ الْجُنُودِ﴾: fāʿil (agent), muḍāf to الجنود; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿فِرْعَوْنَ وَثَمُودَ﴾: badal (substitute) for الجنود, and what follows it is conjoined to it.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿بَلِ﴾: a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and transition; ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿فِي تَكْذِيبٍ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:20-20.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle and the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿مِنْ وَرائِهِمْ مُحِيطٌ﴾: [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) محيط; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:21-21.t: ﴿بَلْ﴾: a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and transition; ﴿هُوَ قُرْآنٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); ﴿مَجِيدٌ﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿فِي لَوْحٍ﴾: a second naʿt (adjective) of قرآن; ﴿مَحْفُوظٍ﴾: adjective of لوح.

dervis-irab:1-9.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْبُرُوجِ): the plural of burj, which is originally the corner, fortress, castle, and any lofty building of round or square form, whether standing alone or part of a great structure. Burj is also one of the towers of the sky, which according to the lexicographers are twelve: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius and Pisces. The root of the composition is for appearing, that is, the original meaning of burj is the manifest thing, from tabarruj; then in common usage it became in reality the lofty castle because of its visibility; and what rises of a city's wall is also called burj.
(الْأُخْدُودِ): singular; its plural is akhādīd. Al-khadd (with fatḥa on the khāʾ) has the meaning of al-ukhdūd, and its plural is khudūd; it is a cleft in the earth, or an elongated pit in it, and it is pluralised akhādīd. Al-akhādīd are also the marks of beating with a whip, and from it the akhādīd of the well ropes in the well, which is the effect of their dragging in it. One says of an old man, "he has taken on furrows (qad takhaddada)," meaning his skin has contracted.

* I'rab:
(وَالسَّماءِ ذاتِ الْبُرُوجِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْمَوْعُودِ وَشاهِدٍ وَمَشْهُودٍ): the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive; السَّماءِ is genitive by the wāw of oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear"; ذاتِ الْبُرُوجِ is a naʿt of السَّماءِ; الْيَوْمِ الْمَوْعُودِ is conjoined to السَّماءِ, or is an oath in itself, and what is meant by it is the Day of Resurrection; other things were said, so refer to the longer works. شاهِدٍ and مَشْهُودٍ are likewise conjoined, and what is meant by it is Muḥammad ﷺ; other things were also said. The response to the oath is omitted, and there is disagreement about it. It was said that it is indicated by the words قُتِلَ أَصْحابُ الْأُخْدُودِ, as if it were said, "I swear by these things that they are cursed as the people of the ditch were cursed." It was also said that its beginning is omitted and the implied form is "laqad qutila"; this omission was needed because the well-known view among the grammarians is that a positive, inflecting past verb whose object has not been fronted, when it occurs as the response to an oath, necessarily takes the lām, and it is not permissible to limit oneself to one of them (lām and qad) except when the speech is long; so the implied form is "laqad qutila," and the clause is therefore declarative, not an imprecation. (قُتِلَ أَصْحابُ الْأُخْدُودِ النَّارِ ذاتِ الْوَقُودِ): قُتِلَ is a passive past verb and أَصْحابُ الْأُخْدُودِ is the deputy agent; النَّارِ is a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from الْأُخْدُودِ, because the ditch contains the fire; a pronoun must be implied in the badal of inclusion, the implied form being "the fire in it"; ذاتِ الْوَقُودِ is a naʿt of النَّارِ. There is disagreement about the link, for they stipulated that the badal of inclusion be attached to a pronoun referring to the substituted-for, as they stipulated that in the badal of part from whole, to link the part to its whole. It was said that the link is omitted, attached to something other than the badal, i.e. "the fire in it," and this is the view of the Basrans. It was also said that nothing is implied and the origin is "its fire," and then the definite article stands in for the pronoun, and this is the view of the Kufans. (إِذْ هُمْ عَلَيْها قُعُودٌ وَهُمْ عَلى ما يَفْعَلُونَ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ شُهُودٌ): إذ is an adverbial for past time, attached to قُتِلَ, i.e. they were cursed when they were burnt by the fire while sitting over it in a place overlooking it from the edges of the ditch; هُمْ is a mubtadaʾ; عَلَيْها is attached to قُعُودٌ; قُعُودٌ is the plural of qāʿid, the khabar of هُمْ; and the clause is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; هُمْ is a mubtadaʾ; عَلى ما يَفْعَلُونَ is attached to شُهُودٌ; and شُهُودٌ is their khabar, i.e. on the Day of Resurrection they will bear witness to what they did to the believers. It was also said that ʿalā means "with," and shuhūd means presence, so the meaning is that "they were present at the torment inflicted on the believers, not softening toward them because of the hardness of their hearts"; this construction is more in keeping with the arrangement of the Qur'an, and Abū Nuwās followed it when he said:
أنت على ما بك من قدرة ... فلست مثل الفضل بالواجد
(For all the power you have, you are not like al-Faḍl in finding means.) «[Translator's note: the sense of this verse as given in the source is obscure; the gloss is tentative.]»
In that case it is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. at the time of their doing it to the believers. (وَما نَقَمُوا مِنْهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ): the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial; ما is negative; نَقَمُوا is a past verb with its agent; مِنْهُمْ is attached to نَقَمُوا; إلا is a particle of restriction; أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of an accusative, the object of نَقَمُوا, i.e. they found no fault with them and denied nothing but faith. More elaboration of this meaning will come in the section on Rhetoric. They expressed it with the imperfect in يُؤْمِنُوا although faith had occurred in them in the past, because their torturing them and denying them was not for the past faith but for its permanence, firmly rooted in their breasts, as if it were said, "except their continuing in their faith." بِاللَّهِ is attached to يُؤْمِنُوا; الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ are two adjectives of اللَّهِ; He mentioned the attributes by which He deserves to be worshipped and believed in by every creature, among them might (ʿizza) and the bestowing of favour for which He deserves praise. (الَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ): الَّذِي is a third naʿt; لَهُ is a fronted khabar and مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ a deferred mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause has no position because it is a ṣila; اللَّهُ is a mubtadaʾ and شَهِيدٌ its khabar; عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ is attached to شَهِيدٌ.

* Rhetoric:
In «وما نقموا منهم إلا أن يؤمنوا بالله العزيز الحميد» there is the art of emphasising praise by what resembles blame (tawkīd al-madḥ bi-mā yushbih al-dhamm), which was alluded to in Sūrat al-Māʾida. It is that a praise attribute be excepted from a negated blame attribute, or that a praise attribute be affirmed for something and then an exception particle follows, followed by another praise attribute. Of the first kind is the verse of al-Nābigha in praise of the Ghassānids:
ولا عيب فيهم غير أنّ سيوفهم ... بهنّ فلول من قرع الكتائب
(There is no fault in them except that their swords are notched from striking the battalions.)
and the saying of Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt, who borrowed the Qur'anic wording and gazed at the sky of its eloquence:
ما نقموا من أمية إلا ... أنهم يحملون إن غضبوا
(They found no fault with Umayya except that they bear with forbearance when they are angry.)
and from it the saying of Ibn Nubāta al-Miṣrī:
ولا عيب فيه غير أني قصدته ... فأنستني الأيام أهلا وموطنا
(There is no fault in him except that I made for him, and the days made me forget family and homeland.)
and the saying of al-Maʿarrī:
تعدّ ذنوبي عند قوم كثيرة ... ولا ذنب لي إلا العلا والفضائل
(My sins are counted many among some people, yet I have no sin except loftiness and virtues.)
As for the second kind, it is rare in poetry, and from it is the saying of one of them:
ما فيك من الجمال سوى ... أنك من أقبح القبيحات
(There is nothing of beauty in you except that you are among the ugliest of the ugly.)

dervis-irab:10-22.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فَتَنُوا): they tormented; what is meant here is that they burnt them with fire. One says fatantu al-shayʾ when I burnt it with fire, and the Arabs say fatana fulān al-dīnār when he put it in the furnace to see its quality. In al-Mukhtār: "al-fitna is testing and trial. You say fatana al-dhahab yaftinuhu (with kasra), fitnatan and also maftūnan, when he put it in the fire to see its quality; and dīnār maftūn. Allah the Exalted said ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ فَتَنُوا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ﴾, i.e. they burnt them. The goldsmith is called al-fattān, and so is Satan. Al-Khalīl said: al-fatn is burning; Allah the Exalted said ﴿يَوْمَ هُمْ عَلَى النَّارِ يُفْتَنُونَ﴾." The wording of al-Qāmūs: "al-fatn (with fatḥa) is kind and condition, and from it al-ʿaysh fatnān, i.e. two colours, sweet and bitter; and burning, and from it ﴿عَلَى النَّارِ يُفْتَنُونَ﴾. Al-fitna (with kasra) is experience, like al-maftūn, and from it ﴿بِأَيِّكُمُ الْمَفْتُونُ﴾; and your admiration of a thing; fatanahu yaftinuhu fatnan and futūnan and aftanahu; and error, sin, disbelief, scandal, torment, the smelting of gold and silver, misleading, madness, tribulation, wealth, children, and people's differing in opinions. Fatanahu yaftinuhu: he put him into fitna, like fattanahu and aftanahu, so he is muftan and maftūn; and he fell into it (intransitive and transitive, like iftatana in both); and 'fatana ilā al-nisāʾ futūnan and futina ilayhinna (with damma)': he wanted debauchery with them. And, in the pattern of amīr, black rocky ground, plural as in kutub. Al-fattān is the thief and Satan, like al-fātin, and the goldsmith. Al-fattānān are the dirham and the dinar, and Munkar and Nakīr. Al-fatīn is the carpenter, and Fātūn is the baker of Pharaoh, killed by Moses. Al-fitnān are the morning and the evening. Al-fattān (like kitāb) is a covering for a saddle made of leather, and (like ṣāḥib and zubayr) two names. Al-maftūn is the mad." Its commentator said: "Al-maftūn is the mad, and by it the words of Allah the Exalted ﴿بِأَيِّكُمُ الْمَفْتُونُ﴾ were interpreted." Al-Jawharī said: "the bāʾ is redundant and al-maftūn is the fitna, a maṣdar like al-maʿqūd, al-majlūd and al-makhlūf." Ibn Barrī said: "If the bāʾ is redundant then al-maftūn is the human being and not a maṣdar; if you make it non-redundant then al-maftūn is a maṣdar." We have transmitted the whole root only in order to refute an error into which Shaykh al-Jamal fell in his gloss on al-Jalālayn, when he said: "In al-Qāmūs: fatana in this sense is of the pattern kataba, so accordingly it has two patterns." From a reading of what we have written and transmitted from al-Qāmūs this error becomes clear.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ فَتَنُوا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَتُوبُوا فَلَهُمْ عَذابُ جَهَنَّمَ وَلَهُمْ عَذابُ الْحَرِيقِ): a resumptive utterance, introduced to mention first the threat to the criminals and then to follow it with mention of what has been prepared for the believers. إن is a particle resembling the verb, and الَّذِينَ its noun; the clause فَتَنُوا is the ṣila of الَّذِينَ with no position; الْمُؤْمِنِينَ is a direct object and الْمُؤْمِناتِ is conjoined to الْمُؤْمِنِينَ; ثُمَّ is a conjunction of sequence with delay; لَمْ is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; يَتُوبُوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لَمْ, and the clause is conjoined to فَتَنُوا. ثُمَّ was used only because repentance is accepted however long it is delayed and extended in time. فَلَهُمْ: the fāʾ is a link to an implied condition understood from the mubtadaʾ; لَهُمْ is a fronted khabar and عَذابُ جَهَنَّمَ a deferred mubtadaʾ; لَهُمْ is a fronted khabar and عَذابُ الْحَرِيقِ a deferred mubtadaʾ; the clause فَلَهُمْ عَذابُ جَهَنَّمَ is the khabar of إن الَّذِينَ فَتَنُوا. (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ ذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْكَبِيرُ): a resumptive utterance as before, introduced to mention what has been prepared for the believers; إن and its noun; the clause آمَنُوا is the ṣila of الَّذِينَ and the clause عَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ is conjoined to the ṣila, within its scope; لَهُمْ is a fronted khabar and جَنَّاتٌ a deferred mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the khabar of إن الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا; the clause تَجْرِي is a naʿt of جَنَّاتٌ; مِنْ تَحْتِهَا is attached to تَجْرِي; الْأَنْهارُ is the agent; ذلِكَ is a mubtadaʾ, الْفَوْزُ the khabar and الْكَبِيرُ a naʿt. The demonstrative is used to draw attention to what was mentioned of their possession of Paradise and their deserving it, and the lām of distance is brought in to signal the height of its rank in excellence. (إِنَّ بَطْشَ رَبِّكَ لَشَدِيدٌ): likewise a resumptive utterance, introduced to console the Prophet for what he endures from the disbelievers of his people, and that their affair is fettered and their plotting will vanish. إن and its noun; the shifted lām; شَدِيدٌ is its khabar. (إِنَّهُ هُوَ يُبْدِئُ وَيُعِيدُ): إن and its noun; هُوَ is a mubtadaʾ, the clause يُبْدِئُ is the khabar of هُوَ, and the clause is the khabar of إن; it is also permissible for هُوَ to be a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) and the clause يُبْدِئُ the khabar of إنه; وَيُعِيدُ is conjoined to يُبْدِئُ. That is, whoever is able to originate and bring into being is able, by nature and self-evidence, to restore. (وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الْوَدُودُ ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ فَعَّالٌ لِما يُرِيدُ): the wāw is a conjunction; هُوَ is a mubtadaʾ; الْغَفُورُ and what follows are khabars. By this verse the grammarians argue for multiple khabars. Al-Zamakhsharī took another route, saying: "فَعَّالٌ is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; it was said faʿʿāl only because what He wills and does is exceedingly abundant." Al-Farrāʾ said: it is nominative by repetition and resumption because it is purely indefinite. (هَلْ أَتاكَ حَدِيثُ الْجُنُودِ؟ فِرْعَوْنَ وَثَمُودَ؟ بَلِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فِي تَكْذِيبٍ): a resumptive utterance, introduced to confirm His seizing and containing a consolation for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, i.e. "has there come to you, Muḥammad, the news of the disbelieving hosts who denied their prophets?" It was said that هَلْ means "qad"; it was also said that it is an interrogative of affirmation and wonder. أَتاكَ is a past verb with a direct object; حَدِيثُ الْجُنُودِ is the agent; فِرْعَوْنَ وَثَمُودَ is a badal from الْجُنُودِ with an omitted muḍāf, because by Pharaoh he meant him and his people; بَلْ is a particle of transitional rejection to what is severer; الَّذِينَ is a mubtadaʾ and فِي تَكْذِيبٍ its khabar. More of its meaning will come in the section on Rhetoric. (وَاللَّهُ مِنْ وَرائِهِمْ مُحِيطٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; اللَّهُ is a mubtadaʾ; مِنْ وَرائِهِمْ is attached to مُحِيطٌ; مُحِيطٌ is the khabar of اللَّهُ. (بَلْ هُوَ قُرْآنٌ مَجِيدٌ فِي لَوْحٍ مَحْفُوظٍ)
بَلْ is a particle of transitional rejection, from the severity of their disbelief to the description of the Qur'an; هُوَ is a mubtadaʾ; قُرْآنٌ is the khabar and مَجِيدٌ an adjective, i.e. it swims alone in eloquence and clear expression; فِي لَوْحٍ is a second adjective and مَحْفُوظٍ is an adjective of لَوْحٍ.

* Rhetoric:
1- In «إن بطش ربك لشديد» he brought the denial-directed statement (al-khabar al-inkārī), which is the emphasis of the speech as obligatory for the one who denies; and he emphasised the speech with إن and the lām.
2- In «بل الذين كفروا في تكذيب» there is a mujāz mursal whose relation is containment by the contained (ḥāliyya), because denial is one of the meanings and a person does not dwell in it; he dwells only in its place; so using "denial" for its place is a figurative use in which the contained is named and the container meant, and its relation is ḥāliyya. He turned away from "they deny" to place them in denial, and that because of its severity it encompassed them as the sea encompasses the drowning man and the bracelet the wrist; at the same time he brought "denial" indefinite to indicate its magnification and the terror of its affair.

* Benefits:
The khabar of a single mubtadaʾ may be multiple, so there is more than one, because the khabar is like the naʿt, so multiplicity is permissible. Ibn Mālik pointed to this in al-Khulāṣa, saying: "And they gave information with two or more about one, as in 'they are noble poets.'"
(وأخبروا باثنين أو بأكثرا ... عن واحد كهم سراة شعرا)
This is regular in two cases. One is that it be multiple in wording and not in meaning, as in "the pomegranate is sweet-sour," because the meaning of the two khabars returns to one thing, as both mean "mizz" (tart); so they are in the position of a single noun. The second is that it be multiple in wording and in meaning, as in "Zayd is a scribe, a poet." The criterion of the first is that it is not permissible to conjoin one of the two khabars to the other, because they are in the position of a single noun; and the criterion of the second is that it is permissible to conjoin the second to the first or not to conjoin.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلسَّمَآءِ ذَاتِ ٱلْبُرُوجِ﴾.
They differed over البروج. They said: they are the stars; and they said: they are the constellations (البروج) in which the sun and the known planets run — twelve constellations; and they said: they are palaces in the sky. And Allah knows best what is correct in that.

farraa:2-3.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْمَوْعُودِ﴾.
They mentioned that it is the Resurrection. ﴿وَشَاهِدٍ﴾: Friday; ﴿وَمَشْهُودٍٍ﴾: the Day of ʿArafa. It is also said: the witness (الشاهد) is also the Day of Resurrection; as though He said: by the promised day and the witness, so that الشاهد is made part of [the description of] الموعود, following it in its genitive.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قُتِلَ أَصْحَابُ ٱلأُخْدُودِ﴾.
It is said in the exegesis that the response (jawāb) to the oath is in His saying "قُتِلَ", just as the response to ﴿وَالشّمسِ وَضُحَاها﴾ is in His saying: ﴿قَدْ أفْلَحَ﴾. That is in the exegesis; but we have not found the Arabs leaving an oath without a lām by which it is met, or "لا", or "إنّ", or "ما". If that is so, then it is as though it is one of those in which the response was left out; then the place of the response was resumed with a statement (khabar), as was said: يأيها الإنسان, in much of the language.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ٱلأُخْدُودِ﴾.
There was a king who dug trenches in the ground for a people, then gathered firewood in them and kindled fires in them, and burned a people with them; and those who dug them sat around them. Then Allah raised the fire up to the disbelievers who had dug them, and it burned them, while the believers were saved from it. That is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَهُمْ عَذَابُ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ (10) in the Hereafter, ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَذابُ الْحَرِيقِ﴾ (10) in this world. It is also said: it burned those who were in it, and those above it were saved.
The one who holds this argued from His saying: ﴿وَهُمْ عَلَى مَا يَفْعَلُونَ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ شُهُودٌ﴾ (7). The first opinion is closer to correct, because of His saying: ﴿فَلَهُمْ عَذَابُ جَهنَّمَ، ولَهُمْ عَذَابُ الْحَرِيقِ﴾, and His saying in describing those who believed: ﴿ذَلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْكَبِيرُ﴾ (11). He says: they won safety from the punishment of the disbelievers and the punishment of the Hereafter — how great a triumph that is!
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُتِلَ أَصْحَابُ ٱلأُخْدُودِ﴾.
He says: the fire killed them. If it were read: "النارُ ذاتُ الوَقُودِ" in the nominative, it would be correct. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read: ﴿وكَذَلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِكَثِيرٍ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ قَتْلَ أَوْلاَدِهِمْ شُرَكَاؤُهم﴾,
putting الشركاء in the nominative by repeating the verb [implicitly]: their partners made it seem fair to them. Likewise His saying: ﴿قُتِلَ أَصْحَابُ ٱلأُخْدُودِ﴾: the fire full of fuel killed them. Whoever puts it in the genitive — "النارِ ذاتِ الْوَقُودِ", which is in the reading of the general public — makes the fire to be the trench, since the fire was in it, as though He said: the people of the fire full of fuel were killed.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذُو ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱلْمَجِيدُ﴾.
Yaḥyā [ibn Waththāb] and his companions put it in the genitive.
Some put it in the nominative, making it an attribute of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He; and its genitive makes it an attribute of the Throne, just as He said: ﴿بَلْ هُوَ قُرْآنٌ مَجِيدٌ﴾ (21), describing the Qurʾān with glory.
Likewise His saying: ﴿فِى لَوْحٍ مَّحْفُوظٍ﴾ (22):
whoever puts it in the genitive makes it an attribute of the Tablet, and whoever puts it in the nominative makes it belong to the Qurʾān. Shayba and Abū Jaʿfar, the two Medinans, put المحفوظ in the nominative.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: His saying «واليوم»: a noun conjoined to «السماء».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The clause «قتل» is the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), and «قتل» is a statement, not an imprecation.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: «النار» is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from {الأُخْدُودِ}, and the pronoun referring back to what is substituted for is implied (muqaddar), i.e.: the fire in it.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: «إذ»: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) {قُتِلَ}, and the clause «هم عليها قعود» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the preposition «عليها» is attached to «قعود».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: (وهم على ما يفعلون بالمؤمنين شهود) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The preposition «على» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «شهود».

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The clause «وما نقموا» is conjoined to the clause «هم شهود», and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «نقموا». «العزيز الحميد» are two naʿts (adjectives).

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: «الذي»: a third naʿt (adjective) of the Majestic Name; the clause «والله شهيد» is resumptive; the preposition «على كل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «شهيد»

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The fāʾ in «فلهم» is redundant (zāʾida); the fāʾ entered because of the sense of condition contained in the mubtadaʾ (subject), and its being abrogated by «إنَّ» does no harm; the clause «لهم عذاب» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن», and the clause «ولهم عذاب» is conjoined to the clause «لهم عذاب».

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «لهم جنات» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ»; the clause «ذلك الفوز الكبير» is resumptive, and «الفوز» is the khabar of the demonstrative.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: (إن بطش ربك لشديد) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: «هو» is tawkīd (emphasis) of the hāʾ in «إنه», and the clause «إنه يبدئ» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The clause «وهو الغفور» is conjoined to the clause «إنه يبدئ»; «الودود» is a second khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: «ذو» is a third khabar (predicate) of «هو»; «المجيد» is a fourth khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: «فَعَّال»: fifth khabar (predicate); the lām is redundant (zāʾida) for strengthening (taqwiya), and «ما» is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: (هل أتاك حديث الجنود) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: «فرعون»: badal (substitute) of {الْجُنُودِ}; the implied form is: the hosts of Pharaoh.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: (بل الذين كفروا في تكذيب) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: (والله من ورائهم محيط) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The preposition «من ورائهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); «محيط» is the khabar of the Majestic Name.

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The preposition «في لوح» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a second naʿt (adjective) of {قُرْآنٌ}.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: (والسماء ذات البروج): its answer is (قتل أصحاب الأخدود), i.e. "surely were killed" (لقتل). It is also said that its answer is (إن بطش ربك لشديد); and also said that the answer is omitted.

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying (واليوم الموعود): (الموعود) is a naʿt (adjective) of (اليوم), and there is an omitted pronoun there by which the adjective is completed, its implied form being "promised of it" (الموعود به). Were it not for that, the adjective would not be sound, since there would be no pronoun in its adjective referring back to the qualified noun.

mekki-muskil:5-5.t: His saying (النار ذات الوقود): (النار) is a badal (substitute) from (الأخدود), and it is the badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl). The Kufans said it is genitive by proximity (al-jiwār). Some of the Kufans said it is a badal, but its implied form is "the people of the trench were killed — its fire", then the alif and lām became a substitute for the pronoun. Some of the Basrans took its implied form as "the people of the fire that was in it were killed".

mekki-muskil:15-15.t: His saying (ذو العرش المجيد): whoever reads it in the genitive makes it a naʿt (adjective) of (العرش). It is also said that it is not permissible for it to be a naʿt of (العرش), because it is one of the attributes of Allah, exalted be His mention; it is only a naʿt of (الرب) in His saying (إن بطش ربك لشديد). Whoever reads it in the nominative makes it a naʿt of (ذو), or a khabar (predicate) after a khabar.

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying (فعال لما يريد): nominative with an implied (هو), or as a khabar (predicate) after a khabar, or as a badal (substitute) from what precedes it, i.e. from (ذو العرش).

mekki-muskil:18-18.t: His saying (فرعون وثمود): a badal (substitute) from (الجنود), in the position of the genitive, or in the position of the accusative with "I mean" (أعني). Both are diptotes: because of definiteness and foreignness in (فرعون), and femininity and definiteness in (ثمود), since it is the name of the tribe.

mekki-muskil:22-22.t: His saying (محفوظ): whoever reads it in the nominative makes it a naʿt (adjective) of (القرآن), and whoever reads it in the genitive makes it a naʿt of (اللوح).

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿والسماء﴾: the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive, and al-samāʾ is a noun in the genitive by the wāw of the oath, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "uqsimu" (I swear).
﴿ذات﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of al-samāʾ, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the kasra.
﴿البروج﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive, the sign of the genitive being the kasra. The clause "uqsimu bi-l-samāʾ" has no grammatical position because it is initial (ibtidāʾiyya).

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿واليوم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and al-yawm is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to al-samāʾ, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿الموعود﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿يوم﴾, genitive by the kasra.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿وشاهد﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and shāhid is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿ومشهود﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and mashhūd is conjoined to what precedes it, genitive by the kasra.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿قتل﴾: qutila is a passive past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿أصحاب﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿الأخدود﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive by the kasra. The clause ﴿قتل أصحاب الأخدود﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿النار﴾: al-nār is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from al-ukhdūd, genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra; a pronoun must be supplied for the badal ishtimāl, the implied form being "al-nār fīhi" (the fire in it).
﴿ذات﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿النار﴾, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the kasra.
﴿الوقود﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive, the sign of its genitive being the kasra.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿إذ﴾: an adverb for past time indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قتل﴾.
﴿هم﴾: a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿عليها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿قعود﴾.
﴿قعود﴾: khabar (predicate) of hum, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma. The clause ﴿هم عليها قعود﴾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿وهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and hum is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿على﴾: a preposition.
﴿ما﴾: maṣdar-forming, or a relative noun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive by ﴿على﴾; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿شهود﴾.
﴿يفعلون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿بالمؤمنين﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition and al-muʾminīn is a genitive noun, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
﴿شهود﴾: khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ ﴿هم﴾, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma. The clause ﴿هم على ما يفعلون بالمؤمنين شهود﴾ is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to ﴿هم عليها قعود﴾, and the clause ﴿يفعلون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and mā is a negative particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿نقموا﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿منهم﴾: min is a preposition and hum is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نقموا﴾.
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿أن﴾: a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿يؤمنوا﴾: an imperfect verb in the subjunctive (manṣūb), the sign of its subjunctive being the dropping of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil. The interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أن يؤمنوا﴾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿نقموا﴾.
﴿بالله﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition and the Name of Majesty ﴿الله﴾ is a genitive noun, the sign of the genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿يؤمنوا﴾.
﴿العزيز﴾: a first naʿt (adjective) of the Name of Majesty ﴿الله﴾, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the kasra.
﴿الحميد﴾: a second naʿt of the Name of Majesty ﴿الله﴾, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the kasra. The clause ﴿ما نقموا﴾ is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to ﴿هم على ما يفعلون بالمؤمنين شهود﴾, and the clause ﴿يؤمنوا﴾ is the ṣila of the particle-relative ﴿أن﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿الذي﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the genitive as a third naʿt (adjective) of the Name of Majesty ﴿الله﴾.
﴿له﴾: the lām is a preposition and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿ملك﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿السماوات﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive by the kasra.
﴿والأرض﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and al-arḍ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to al-samāwāt, genitive by the kasra.
﴿والله﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the Name of Majesty ﴿الله﴾ is mubtadaʾ, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿على﴾: a preposition.
﴿كل﴾: a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿شهيد﴾.
﴿شيء﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the kasra.
﴿شهيد﴾: khabar of the Name of Majesty ﴿الله﴾, nominative by the ḍamma. The clause ﴿له ملك السماوات والأرض﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position, and the clause ﴿والله على كل شيء شهيد﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿إن﴾: a particle of emphasis and accusative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿الذين﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as the noun (ism) of inna.
﴿فتنوا﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿المؤمنين﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural.
﴿والمؤمنات﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and al-muʾmināt is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to al-muʾminīn, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra [Translator's note: so in the source; as it is conjoined to an accusative mafʿūl bihi, "accusative by the kasra" would be expected].
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction.
﴿لم﴾: a particle of negation and jussive.
﴿يتوبوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil.
﴿فلهم﴾: the fāʾ is connective (ṣila); lahum: the lām is a preposition and hum is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿عذاب﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿جهنم﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive by the fatḥa because it is a diptote, on account of being a proper name and feminine.
﴿ولهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; lahum: the lām is a preposition and hum is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted, fronted khabar.
﴿عذاب﴾: mubtadaʾ, nominative by the ḍamma.
﴿الحريق﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive by the kasra. The clause ﴿إن الذين فتنوا المؤمنين والمؤمنات﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; the clause ﴿فَتَنُوا﴾ [is the ṣila of] the relative noun, with no grammatical position; the clause ﴿لم يتوبوا﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿فتنوا﴾; ﴿لهم عذاب جهنم﴾ is in the position of the nominative as khabar of inna; and ﴿لهم عذاب الحريق﴾ is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause ﴿لهم عذاب جهنم﴾.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿إن﴾: a particle of emphasis and accusative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿الذين﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as the noun (ism) of inna.
﴿آمنوا﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿وعملوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ʿamilū is a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil.
﴿الصالحات﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the kasra because it is a plural ending in alif and tāʾ.
﴿لهم﴾: the lām is a preposition and hum is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿جنات﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿تجري﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ.
﴿من﴾: a preposition.
﴿تحتها﴾: a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra, and ﴿ها﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿تجري﴾.
﴿الأنهار﴾: fāʿil, nominative by the ḍamma.
﴿ذلك﴾: dhā is a demonstrative indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address.
﴿الفوز﴾: khabar, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿الكبير﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿الفوز﴾, nominative by the ḍamma. The clause ﴿إن الذين آمنوا...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; the clause ﴿عملوا﴾ is conjoined to ﴿آمنوا﴾, with no grammatical position; ﴿لهم جنات﴾ is in the position of the nominative as khabar of inna; and the clause ﴿ذلك الفوز﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿إن﴾: a particle of emphasis and accusative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿بطش﴾: the noun (ism) of inna, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿ربك﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive, and the kāf is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿لشديد﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis, and shadīd is khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma. The clause ﴿إن بطش ربك لشديد﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position, or it is the answer to the oath at the beginning of the sura.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿إنه﴾: inna is a particle of emphasis and accusative indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative as the noun (ism) of inna.
﴿هو﴾: a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿يبدئ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being ﴿هو﴾.
﴿ويعيد﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and yuʿīd is an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma, and the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "huwa". The clause ﴿إنه هو يبدئ...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; the clause ﴿يبدئ...﴾ is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of inna; and the clause ﴿يعيد﴾ is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to ﴿يبدئ﴾.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿وهو﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and huwa is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿الغفور﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿الودود﴾: a second khabar, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma. The clause ﴿هو الغفور﴾ is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause ﴿يبدئ﴾.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿ذو﴾: a third khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿هو﴾, nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw because it is one of the six nouns.
﴿العرش﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive by the kasra.
﴿المجيد﴾: a fourth khabar of the mubtadaʾ ﴿هو﴾, nominative by the ḍamma.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿فعال﴾: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿لما﴾: the lām is a preposition. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa), indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the genitive by the lām in form, and in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿فعال﴾.
﴿يريد﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma. The clause ﴿يريد﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position, or it is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ما﴾.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿هل﴾: an interrogative particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿أتاك﴾: a past verb indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif, and the kāf is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿حديث﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿الجنود﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive, the sign of its genitive being the kasra. The clause ﴿أتاك...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿فرعون﴾: a badal (substitute) from ﴿الجنود﴾, genitive (majrūr) by the fatḥa because it is a diptote, on account of being a proper name and foreign.
﴿وثمود﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and thamūd is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿فرعون﴾, genitive like it by the fatḥa, on account of being a proper name and feminine.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿بل﴾: a particle of transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī).
﴿الذين﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿كفروا﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿في﴾: a preposition.
﴿تكذيب﴾: a noun in the genitive by ﴿في﴾, the sign of the genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of alladhīna. The clause ﴿الذين كفروا في تكذيب﴾ has no grammatical position, being resumptive, and the clause ﴿كفروا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿والله﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or a conjunction, and the Name of Majesty ﴿الله﴾ is mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿من﴾: a preposition.
﴿ورائهم﴾: warāʾ is a noun in the genitive by ﴿من﴾, the sign of the genitive being the kasra, and hum is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) muḥīṭ.
﴿محيط﴾: khabar (predicate) of the Name of Majesty ﴿الله﴾, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma. The clause ﴿الله من ورائهم محيط﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or it is conjoined to the clause ﴿الذين كفروا في تكذيب﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿بل﴾: a particle of transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī).
﴿هو﴾: a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿قرآن﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿مجيد﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿قرآن﴾, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma. The clause ﴿هو قرآن مجيد﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿في﴾: a preposition.
﴿لوح﴾: a genitive noun by the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second naʿt (adjective) of ﴿قرآن﴾, genitive by the kasra [Translator's note: so in the source; since ﴿قرآن﴾ is nominative, the words "genitive by the kasra" can only describe ﴿لوح﴾ itself].
﴿محفوظ﴾: a naʿt of ﴿لوح﴾, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: وَالسَّماءِ is genitive by the wāw of oath. ذاتِ الْبُرُوجِ is a naʿt (adjective) of السماء. The grammarians differed about the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam). Some of them said: it is omitted. Some said: the implied form is "surely (لـ) the people of the ditch were killed", the lām being omitted. Some said: the answer is إِنَّ بَطْشَ رَبِّكَ لَشَدِيدٌ (12). Abū Ḥātim said: the implied form is "the people of the ditch were killed, by the sky with its constellations". Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a clear mistake. The grammarians are agreed that والله قام زيد is not permissible in the sense of قام زيد والله. The basis of this in Arabic is that when the oath is placed at the beginning, it may not be cancelled (ilghāʾ), nor may it be intended to be placed later; when it comes in the middle or at the end, it may be cancelled. There is a fifth answer on it: that the implied form is وَالسَّماءِ ذاتِ الْبُرُوجِ (1) إِنَّ الَّذِينَ فَتَنُوا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ [the verse: 10], and what intervenes between them is conjoined [to the oath] and a preparation for the oath. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: Know that the oath may be reinforced by what confirms the statement before the thing sworn to is mentioned, and then what the oath falls on is mentioned. Of that kind is وَالسَّماءِ ذاتِ الْبُرُوجِ (1); then He mentioned the story of the people of the ditch, and the oath falls only on His saying إِنَّ بَطْشَ رَبِّكَ لَشَدِيدٌ (12).

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ فَتَنُوا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ: Qatāda said: [i.e.] they burnt them. ثُمَّ لَمْ يَتُوبُوا, i.e. from that deed of theirs. فَلَهُمْ عَذابُ جَهَنَّمَ وَلَهُمْ عَذابُ الْحَرِيقِ: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq said: they were burnt in this world; Abū al-ʿĀliya said the same; and they will have the punishment of Hell in the Hereafter.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا, i.e. they affirmed the oneness of Allah, glory be to Him. [Translator's note: the source reads «أمروا», apparently a misprint for «أقرّوا».] وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ: they kept to the command and prohibition of Allah. لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ: these are rivers of water, and rivers of wine, milk and honey. ذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْكَبِيرُ, i.e. attaining what they sought.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: That is, as He seized the people of the ditch — a warning of His punishment.

nahhas-irab:13-14.t: إِنَّهُ هُوَ يُبْدِئُ وَيُعِيدُ (13): there are two views on its meaning. Ibn Zayd said: He begins the creation of creatures, then brings them back on the Day of Resurrection. From Ibn ʿAbbās: He begins the punishment in this world, then repeats it on them in the Hereafter. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is closer to the meaning, because the context of the story is that they were burnt in this world and they will have the punishment of Hell. If it is said: How does this agree with the ḥadīth [that] whoever is punished in this world, Allah is too generous to repeat the punishment on him? The answer to this is that his punishment on the Day of Resurrection is reduced by the amount that befell him in this world, not that all of it is removed from him on the Day of Resurrection. What indicates that answer related from Ibn ʿAbbās is that after it comes وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الْوَدُودُ (14), a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: [الْمَجِيدُ] in the nominative is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدِ in the genitive. [Translator's note: the source prints this reading with a ḍamma («الْمَجِيدُ»), though it describes the genitive.] Some grammarians consider the genitive unlikely, because المجيد is known as one of the attributes of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, so contiguity [i.e. genitive by proximity] is not permissible in the Book of Allah; indeed, according to the school of Sībawayh it is not permissible in prose or poetry, and it is only a mistake in their saying هذا جحر ضبّ خرب ("this is the hole of a ruined lizard"), and its counterpart in error is iqwāʾ [a fault of rhyme]. [Translator's note: the source reads «الجواب» here; from the context, «الجوار» (contiguity) is meant.] But the reading with the genitive is permissible not on the basis of contiguity, on the basis that the implied form is "the seizing of your Lord", الْمَجِيدِ being a naʿt (adjective) [of ربك].

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: [فَعَّالٌ] may be a khabar (predicate) after a khabar, as Sībawayh reported: هذا حلو حامض ("this is sweet-sour"). It may also be nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject). It cannot be a naʿt (adjective), because it is indefinite; but it may also be a badal (substitute).

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: That is, those who formed into armies (tajannadū) to disobey Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, and to reject His messengers.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: A mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and likewise

nahhas-irab:2-3.t: وَالْيَوْمِ الْمَوْعُودِ (2): [its wāw] is a wāw of conjunction, not a wāw of oath; and likewise وَشاهِدٍ وَمَشْهُودٍ (3). Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned its meaning. It has also been said: on the Day of Resurrection people will not be free of a witness and something witnessed, so the meaning is "and by the Lord of people".

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: and likewise [Translator's note: this entry and the previous one are left incomplete in the source.]

nahhas-irab:21-22.t: بَلْ هُوَ قُرْآنٌ مَجِيدٌ (21) فِي لَوْحٍ مَحْفُوظٍ (22) in the genitive is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, Yaḥyā, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī. It is what is well known in the ḥadīth and the reports, that it is the Preserved Tablet, i.e. preserved from anything being added to or taken away from what Allah inscribed in it. Nāfiʿ and Ibn Muḥayṣin read فِي لَوْحٍ مَحْفُوظٌ in the nominative, as a naʿt (adjective) of قرآن, i.e. "Rather, it is a glorious Qur'an, preserved from being changed, added to or taken away from; Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, has preserved it from these things". [Translator's note: the source prints the nominative reading with the genitive vowel «مَحْفُوظٍ»; it is supplied here according to the description.] So the reading in the nominative is also sound. For this reason many scholars said: whoever claims that something of the Qur'an has remained [outside it] is rejecting Allah and is a disbeliever thereby; and the text about which there is no disagreement is إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحافِظُونَ [al-Ḥijr: 9], of which «محفوظ» in the nominative is the counterpart.

nahhas-irab:4-5.t:
النَّارِ ذاتِ الْوَقُودِ (5) is genitive as a badal al-ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion). There are two implied forms in it: one of them is "its fire", the alif and lām being a compensation for the pronoun; the other is "the fire that is in it". This is the badal al-ishtimāl. On the meaning of قُتِلَ أَصْحابُ الْأُخْدُودِ (4) there are two views: one is that they are the believers whom the disbelievers killed; the other is that they are the disbelievers, and the meaning of قتلوا is then "they were cursed" or "they were destroyed". «The grammarians» permitted قتل أصحاب الأخدود النارُ ذات الوقود in the nominative, as Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read وَكَذلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِكَثِيرٍ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ قَتْلُ أَوْلادِهِمْ شُرَكاؤُهُمْ [al-Anʿām: 137]. [Translator's note: the source prints this verse in the standard vocalisation «زَيَّنَ … قَتْلَ … شُرَكاؤُهُمْ»; al-Sulamī's reading, with the passive verb and nominative «قتلُ», is what the argument requires.] Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a subtle chapter of grammar which Sībawayh mentioned: it is permissible to say ضُرب زيدٌ عمرٌو, because when you say ضُرب زيد ("Zayd was struck") it indicates that he had a striker, and the implied form is "ʿAmr struck him". Likewise قُتِلَ أَصْحابُ الْأُخْدُودِ (4) — the fire killed them. Sībawayh recited: [al-ṭawīl] 554-
ليبك يزيد ضارع لخصومة ... وأشعث ممّن طوّحته الطّوائح
(Let Yazīd be wept for — [by] one humbled in a dispute, and a dishevelled one of those whom calamities have cast away.)
— i.e. one humbled weeps for him. Al-Akhfash said: الوقود with fatḥa is the firewood, and الوقود with ḍamma is the act — he means the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. the kindling.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: Qatāda said: [the ones sitting around it are] the believers. This is according to one of the two interpretations.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: That is, they were not absent.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: وَما نَقَمُوا مِنْهُمْ — one also says نقموا — i.e. they found nothing against them except their faith in Allah, the Mighty [الْعَزِيزِ] in His vengeance, الْحَمِيدِ, i.e. the One praised by His servants for His beautiful acts.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: الَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ is a naʿt (adjective) with a sense of praise, in the position of the genitive. It may also be in the position of the accusative as praise (ʿalā al-madḥ), or in the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject). وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ, i.e. He has witnessed their deeds and the deeds of others and knows them, so as to requite them for them.

safi-cedvel:11-11.t:
* I'rab:
(لهم) is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (جنّات). (من تحتها) is attached to (تجري), with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "beneath its trees". The reference in (ذلك) is to the believers' acquisition of the gardens. (الفوز) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative.
Clause: «إنّ الذين آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).
And the clause: «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين)).
And the clause: «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause آمنوا).
And the clause: «لهم جنّات ... » is in the position of nominative (raf') as the khabar of inna.
And the clause: «تجري ... الأنهار» is in the position of nominative as an naʿt (adjective) of جنّات.
And the clause: «ذلك الفوز ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).

safi-cedvel:12-16.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) of emphasis. (هو) is a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is the clause يبدئ «[Note: Or it is a pronoun borrowed for the position of accusative, as emphasis (tawkīd) of the pronoun that is the noun of inna; the clause هو الغفور is then conjoined to the clause إنّه هو.]». (الواو) is a conjunction. (اللام) is redundant (zāʾida) for reinforcement «[Note: or it is not redundant, being attached to فعّال.]». (ما) is a relative noun, whose remote position is that of a direct object (mafʿūl bihi) of the intensive form فعّال.
Clause: «إنّ بطش ربّك لشديد» has no grammatical position (resumptive) «[Note: Some made it the answer to the oath mentioned at the beginning of the sūra: والسماء ذات ...]».
And the clause: «إنّه هو يبدئ ... » has no grammatical position (causal).
And the clause: «هو يبدئ ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
And the clause: «يبدئ ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of (هو).
And the clause: «يعيد ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يبدئ.
And the clause: «هو الغفور ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause هو يبدئ «[Note: It may be conjoined to the resumptive clause, in which case it has no grammatical position.]».
And the clause: «يريد» has no grammatical position (ṣila of the relative noun (ما)).

safi-cedvel:17-18.t:
* I'rab:
(هل) is a particle of interrogation meaning affirmation (taqrīr) «[Note: or the interrogation expresses wonder ... and it may mean قد.]». (فرعون) is a badal (substitute) for الجنود, genitive; it contains an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the soldiers of Pharaoh".
Clause: «هل أتاك حديث ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).

safi-cedvel:19-20.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) is for transition (iḍrāb intiqālī). (في تكذيب) is attached to the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الذين). (الواو) is a conjunction. (من ورائهم) is attached to (محيط) «[Note: or it is the first khabar and (محيط) a second khabar.]».
Clause: «الذين كفروا في تكذيب» has no grammatical position (resumptive).
And the clause: «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين)).
And the clause: «الله ... محيط» has no grammatical position (conjoined to the resumptive clause).

* Morphology:
(تكذيب) is a regular maṣdar (verbal noun) of the quadriliteral كذّب; its wazn is تفعيل.

* Rhetoric:
Tamthīl (representation): in His words, the Exalted, «مِنْ وَرائِهِمْ مُحِيطٌ».
It is a representation of their not escaping the might of Allah the Exalted, by the fact that what is encompassed cannot slip away from what encompasses it. The meaning is that He, Mighty and Majestic, knows them and has power over them; they cannot frustrate Him nor escape Him, glory be to Him, the Exalted.
Majāz mursal (unrestricted figurative usage): in His words, the Exalted, «بَلِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فِي تَكْذِيبٍ».
The relation of this majāz is "the contained for the container" (ḥāliyya): denial is an abstract notion, and a person does not dwell in it; he dwells only in a place. So using denial for the place is figurative: the thing that dwells (ḥāl) is mentioned and the place (maḥall) is meant; hence its relation is ḥāliyya.

safi-cedvel:21-22.t:
* I'rab:
(في لوح) is attached to a second naʿt (adjective) of قرآن.
Clause: «هو قرآن ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).

safi-cedvel:1-7.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is the wāw of oath; (السماء) is genitive by the wāw, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being أقسم ("I swear"); (النار) is a badal ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) for الأخدود [Note: the pronoun returning to the thing substituted for is omitted, i.e.: the fire in it.] ; (إذ) is an adverb in the position of an accusative, attached to (قتل) ; (ما) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of a genitive, with the returning pronoun omitted.] ; (بالمؤمنين) is attached to (يفعلون) .
The interpreted maṣdar (ما يفعلون..) is in the position of a genitive by (على) , attached to (شهود) .
Clause: « (أقسم) بالسماء ... » has no grammatical position, inceptive.. and the answer to the oath is omitted, its implied form being: "the recompense is true, or will surely befall the unbelievers ...".
And the clause: «قتل أصحاب ... » has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption [Note: if the sentence is declarative, not a performative of supplication, it is itself the answer to the oath, with the lām and قد implied.] .
And the clause: «هم عليها قعود» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of a genitive construct).
And the clause: «هم ... شهود» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause «هم عليها قعود» .
And the clause: «يفعلون ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (ما) .

* Morphology:
(2) الموعود: a passive participle of the triliteral وعد, on the pattern مفعول; it is the Day of Resurrection.
(4) الأخدود: a noun for a cleft in the earth, on the pattern أفعول (with ḍamma on the hamza and sukūn on the fāʾ); the plural is أفاعيل.

* Benefits:
- The People of the Trench:
It is reported from Ṣuhayb that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: There was a king among those before you, who had a sorcerer. When the sorcerer grew old he said to the king: Send me a boy whom I may teach sorcery. On the boy's way there was a monk; he sat with him and was pleased with his words. He would be late in going to the sorcerer and in returning to his family, and he complained of that to the monk, who said to him: Say to the sorcerer: My family detained me, and say to your family: The sorcerer detained me. While the boy was like that, a beast appeared that blocked the road. The boy took a stone and said: O Allah, if the monk's matter is dearer to You, then kill this beast. And the beast died.
He told that to the monk, who gave him glad tidings of good and said to him: You have become better than I, and you will surely be tested, so do not point to me. The boy used to cure the blind from birth and the leper by Allah's permission, and to treat people's illnesses. A blind man who was a companion of the king came to him with gifts and said to him: All this is yours if you heal me. The boy said: It is only Allah who heals you. So he believed in Him, and the king's companion believed; the boy supplicated for him and he was cured. The king asked him how he was healed of his illness, and he told him and said to him: Allah healed me. The king said: Do you have a Lord other than me? The companion said: My Lord and your Lord is Allah. The king did not cease torturing him until he pointed him to the boy, and the king did not cease torturing the boy until he pointed to the monk. The monk was brought, and he demanded that he turn back from his religion, but he refused; so he sawed him from the parting of his head until his two halves fell, and then he did the same to the companion.
Then the king handed the boy to a group of men and entrusted them to throw him from the top of a high mountain. The boy said: O Allah, spare me from them in whatever way You will and however You will. The mountain shook with them and they fell, and he came walking to the king.
The king said to him: What did your companions do? He said: Allah spared me from them. So he handed him to another group and said: Put him in a small boat and take him to the middle of the sea; if he turns back from his religion, well; otherwise throw him into the deep. He said: O Allah, spare me from them in whatever way You will and however You will. The boat capsized with them and they drowned. The boy came walking, and the king asked him about his companions. He said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, spared me from them. He said to the king: You will not kill me until you do what I command you. He said: What is it? He said: Gather the people in one open place, crucify me on the trunk of a palm tree, then take an arrow from my quiver and say: In the name of Allah, the Lord of the boy; then shoot me with it, and then you will kill me. The king did that and struck him with the arrow, saying: In the name of Allah, the Lord of the boy. The arrow landed in his temple, and the boy put his hand on the spot where the arrow landed, and then died. The people said: We believe in the Lord of the boy. It was said to the king: Do you see what you feared? By Allah, it has befallen you. The king ordered a trench to be dug and fires to be kindled in it; whoever did not turn back from his religion was thrown into the fire. A woman was brought with her child, and she hesitated. The boy said to her [Translator's note: the source text says "the boy" here, apparently meaning her child]: O mother, be patient, for you are upon the truth. This ḥadīth is authentic; Muslim recorded it.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: In Najrān there was a king among the kings of Ḥimyar called Yūsuf Dhū Nuwās ibn Sharḥabīl ibn Sharāḥīl, in the interval (fatra) seventy years before the birth of the Prophet ﷺ. In his land there was a boy called ʿAbd Allāh ibn Tāmir, whose father used to hand him over to a teacher who taught him sorcery; and he went on to narrate the same preceding ḥadīth reported by Ṣuhayb.
- Omission of قد:
The Basrans mentioned that a past verb occurring as a ḥāl (circumstantial) must be accompanied by (قد) , either overt, as in His saying, the Exalted (وَما لَكُمْ أَلَّا تَأْكُلُوا مِمَّا ذُكِرَ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ وَقَدْ فَصَّلَ لَكُمْ) , or implicit, as in His saying, the Exalted (أَنُؤْمِنُ لَكَ وَاتَّبَعَكَ الْأَرْذَلُونَ) , i.e. (وقد اتبعك) , and (أَوْ جاؤُكُمْ حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهُمْ) , i.e. قد حصرت. All of them said: the affirmative past verb that answers an oath should be accompanied by the lām and قد, as in His saying, the Exalted (تَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ آثَرَكَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْنا) . It is said concerning His saying, the Exalted: (قُتِلَ أَصْحابُ الْأُخْدُودِ) , in the verse we are dealing with, that it is the answer to the oath with both the lām and قد implied, i.e. (لقد قتل) .

safi-cedvel:8-9.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is a conjunction; (ما) is a negative; (منهم) is attached to (نقموا) , by its implying the sense "they found fault"; (إلّا) is for restriction; (أن) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) particle that puts the verb in the accusative; (بالله) is attached to (يؤمنوا) ; (الحميد) is a second naʿt (adjective) of the divine name.
Clause: «ما نقموا» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause هم.. شهود [Note: in the preceding verse (7) .] .
And the clause: «يؤمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن) .
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يؤمنوا) is in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb نقموا [Note: it may be a badal (substitute) for the implied object, with (إلّا) for exception, i.e. "they resented nothing except their faith", or it is accusative as an exception.] .
9- (الذي) is a relative noun in the position of a genitive, a third naʿt of the divine name [Note: or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هو" (He), the clause being an explanatory resumption.] ; (له) is attached to an advanced khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ملك) ; (الواو) is resumptive; (على كلّ) is attached to (شهيد) ..
And the clause: «له ملك ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي) .
And the clause: «الله ... شهيد» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
The art of reinforcing praise with what resembles blame: in His saying, the Exalted, «وَما نَقَمُوا مِنْهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ» .
An exception that discloses their total freedom from anything that is faulted or denounced, on the pattern of his saying:
ولا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم ... بهن فلول من قراع الكتائب
(There is no fault in them except that their swords are notched from battering the battalions.)
Here a quality of praise has been excepted from a negated quality of blame, and this is what is called reinforcing praise with what resembles blame.

safi-cedvel:10-10.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is redundant (zāʾida), because of the relative noun's resemblance to a condition; (لهم) is attached to an advanced khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (عذاب) in the two places.
Clause: «إنّ الذين فتنوا ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «فتنوا ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين) .
And the clause: «لم يتوبوا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause فتنوا.
And the clause: «لهم عذاب» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of إنّ.
And the clause: «لهم عذاب (the second) » is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the khabar clause.

* Morphology:
(الحريق): a noun for the state of the blazing and kindling of fire; it is used in the verse in the sense of الإحراق ("burning"), i.e. the unbelievers' burning of the believers [Note: that is, "for them is the punishment because of the burning".] ; so it is a ism maṣdar (noun of verbal action), on the pattern فعيل.

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {فَلَهُمْ عَذَابُ}: it is the khabar of «إنَّ الذين», and the fāʾ entered because of the sense of condition contained in the mubtadaʾ; its being governed by «إنَّ» does not harm it, contrary to al-Akhfash. The nominative of «عذابُ» is possible as agent of the preposition-phrase before it, because it occurs as a khabar, and this is the better; and it is possible that it be nominative as a mubtadaʾ.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {الودود}: an intensive form of wudd (affection). Ibn ʿAbbās said: "He is the One who shows affection to His servants through forgiveness." From al-Mubarrad: "He is the one who has no child," and he recited:
4573 - وأَرْكَبُ في الرَّوْعِ خَيْفانَةً ... ذَلولَ الجِماحِ لِقاحاً وَدُوْدا
(In the terror of battle I ride a swift mare, docile in her bolting, a milch-mare, affectionate.)
[Translator's note: the verse number is printed "4573" in the source; the numbering sequence would suggest 4537.] i.e. she has no foal for which she yearns. It is also said: it is faʿūl in the sense of mafʿūl, like al-rakūb and al-ḥalūb, i.e. His righteous servants love Him.

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {المجيد}: the two Kufan masters (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read it in the genitive; it is said it is an adjective of the Throne. It is also said it is an adjective of «ربِّك» in His saying {إِنَّ بَطْشَ رَبِّكَ لَشَدِيدٌ} [البروج: 12]. Makkī said: "It is said that it cannot be an adjective of the Throne because it is among the attributes of Allah the Exalted." The rest read it in the nominative as a khabar after a khabar. It is also said that it is an adjective of «ذو». Some took this verse as evidence for multiple khabars. Whoever denies this says: because the two are in the sense of one khabar, i.e. combining these noble attributes; or each of them is a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ.

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {فِرْعَوْنَ وَثَمُودَ}: it may be a badal of «الجنود»; in that case the badal ought to match the word it substitutes for in being plural, so it is said: it is on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the armies of Pharaoh". It is also said that Pharaoh and his people are meant, and mentioning him sufficed in place of mentioning them, because they are his followers. It may also be accusative with an implied "I mean", because when it does not match what precedes it, it must be cut off (qaṭʿ).

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying: {قُرْآنٌ مَّجِيدٌ}: the majority read «مَجيد» as following «قرآن». Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read it with «قرآن» annexed to «مَجيد»; it is said that it is on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the Qur'an of a glorious Lord", as in:
4538 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولكنَّ الغِنى رَبٌّ غفورُ
(… but wealth is a Lord, Forgiving.)
i.e. the wealth of a forgiving Lord. It is also said: rather it is an annexation of the qualified noun to its attribute, so the two readings coincide; but the Basrans do not allow this, lest it require annexing a thing to itself, and they reinterpret what has been transmitted.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {مَّحْفُوظٍ}: Nāfiʿ read it in the nominative as an adjective of «قرآن»; the rest read it in the genitive as an adjective of «لوحٍ». The majority read the lām with fatḥa; Ibn al-Samayfaʿ and Ibn Yaʿmur read it with ḍamma. al-Zamakhsharī said: "He means the tablet above the seventh heaven, in which the tablet is protected from the reaching of the devils to it." Abū l-Faḍl said: "al-lawḥ is the air (al-hawāʾ)"; al-Zamakhsharī's explanation is closer to the meaning, and it is what Ibn Khālawayh intended.
[Translator's note: the source text ends with a stray closing quotation mark after Ibn Khālawayh.]

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {قُتِلَ}: this is the answer to the oath according to the preferred view, and the lām was omitted; the original is «لَقُتِلَ», as in the poet's saying:
4533 - حَلَفْتُ لها باللَّهِ حَلْفَةَ فاجرٍ ... لَناموا فما إنْ مِنْ حديثٍ ولا صالِ
