(I swore to her by Allah, the oath of a wicked man: "They slept, and there was neither talk nor anyone kindling a fire.")
Its omission is good only because of length, as will come, Allah willing, at His saying {قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن زَكَّاهَا} [الشمس: 9]. It is also said that the implied form is «لقد قُتِلَ», the lām and «قد» having been omitted; on this, His saying «قُتِلَ» is a statement and not an imprecation. It is also said that it is an imprecation, and so it is not the answer. In that case there are several views on the answer. One: that it is His saying {إِنَّ الذين فَتَنُواْ}. Two: His saying {إِنَّ بَطْشَ رَبِّكَ}; al-Mubarrad said this. Three: that it is implied. al-Zamakhsharī said, and he mentioned nothing else: "It is omitted, and {قُتِلَ أَصْحَابُ الأخدود} indicates it, as though it were said: I swear by these things that the disbelievers of Quraysh are accursed as the People of the Trench were cursed." Then he said: "«قُتِل» is an imprecation against them, like His saying {قُتِلَ الإنسان} [عبس: 17]." It is also said that the implied form is «لَتُبْعَثُنَّ» ("you will surely be resurrected").
al-Ḥasan and Ibn Miqsam read «قُتِّلَ» with a doubled tāʾ, for intensity or multiplicity. His saying «الموعودِ» means "that which is promised (of it)", i.e. promised with it. Makkī said: "«الموعود» is an adjective (naʿt) of the day. There is an omitted pronoun there completing it: «الموعودِ به». Were it not for that, the adjective would not be sound, since there is no pronoun returning to the qualified noun from its adjective." End of quotation. It seems he means that the day is something others are promised with, so a pronoun returning to it is needed, because it is "promised with" and not "promised". This is not needed, because it is possible that figurative usage is meant, namely that the day was promised such-and-such, so that it is sound and includes a pronoun returning to it, as though it were said: "and the day on which it was promised that judgment would be passed among creatures".
al-Ukhdūd: a cleft in the earth. al-Zamakhsharī said: "al-Ukhdūd is the khadd in the earth, which is a cleft. Similar to them in form and meaning are al-khaqq and al-ukhqūq, from which comes: «فساخَتْ قوائمُه في أخاقيقِ جِرْذان» ('his legs sank into the burrows of rats')." End of quotation. al-Khadd is originally a verbal noun, and it may apply to the object, which is the cleft itself, whereas al-ukhdūd is a noun for it only. al-Rāghib said: "al-khadd and al-ukhdūd are a long, deep cleft in the earth.
The plural of al-ukhdūd is akhādīd. The origin of that is the two cheeks (khaddayn) of a man, which flank the nose on the right and left. al-Khadd is used metaphorically for the earth and other things, just as 'face' is; and takhaddud al-laḥm is the wasting of flesh from the face of the body." Then the one who has wasted (mutakhaddid) is used for the emaciated, and al-khidād is a brand on the cheek. Another said: al-khadd is called khadd because tears cut furrows (akhādīd) in it, i.e. channels.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {النار}: the majority read it in the genitive, and there are several views on it. One: that it is a badal (substitute) of «الأخدود», a badal al-ishtimāl (inclusive substitute), because the trench includes it; in that case a pronoun is required in it. The Basrans said: it is implied, its implied form being "the fire in it". The Kufans said: the article «أل» stands in place of the pronoun, the implied form being "its fire"; then the pronoun was omitted and «أل» substituted for it. The discussion with them on this has already been given. Two: that it is a badal kull min kull (total substitute), in which case an omitted muḍāf must be assumed, the implied form being "the trench of the fire". Three: that the implied form is "possessor of the fire", because al-ukhdūd is the cleft in the earth; Abū l-Baqāʾ related this. This suggests that «النار» is genitive by annexation to that omitted attribute; when the muḍāf was omitted, the muḍāf ilayhi took its place in the case-ending, and it happened that the omitted word was genitive. His saying "because al-ukhdūd is the cleft" is a justification for the soundness of its being the possessor of a fire; and this is very weak. Four: that «النار» is genitive by proximity (jiwār); Makkī related this from the Kufans. This requires that «النار» was due to take a case other than the genitive and was turned from it to the genitive because of proximity. What the situation requires is that it was turned from the nominative, and what indicates that is that it has been read in an irregular reading as «النارُ» in the nominative; and the nominative is as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the implied form being "their killing was the fire". It is also said: rather it is nominative as agent, the implied form being "the fire killed them", i.e. burned them, and in that case the People of the Trench are the believers.
The majority read «الوَقود» with fatḥa on the wāw; al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ, Abū Ḥaywa and ʿĪsā read it with ḍamma. The two readings and what people said about them were given at the beginning of al-Baqara.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {إِذْ هُمْ}: the operator in «إذ» is either «قُتِلَ أصحابُ», i.e. they were killed at this time; or it is said to be an implied "remember", in which case it is a direct object. The meaning of their sitting over it: / i.e. over what is near it, such as its edge, from which comes the saying of al-Aʿshā:
4534 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وباتَ على النارِ النَّدى والمُحَلَّقُ
(… and generosity and al-Muḥallaq spent the night by the fire.)
The pronoun in «هم» may refer to the believers, and may refer to the disbelievers.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {وَمَا نَقَمُواْ}: the majority read it with fatḥa on the qāf; Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it with kasra. The meaning of that has already been given in al-Māʾida.
His saying: {إِلاَّ أَن يُؤْمِنُواْ} is like, in meaning, the saying:
4535 - ولا عَيْبَ فيها غيرَ شُكْلَةِ عَيْنِها ... كذاك عِتاقُ الطيرِ شُكْلٌ عُيونُها
(There is no fault in her except the reddish tinge of her eye; so too the eyes of noble birds are tinged.)
and like the saying of Qays al-Ruqayyāt:
4536 - ما نَقِموا من بني أُمَيَّةَ إلاَّ ... أنَّهم يَحْلُمُون إنْ غَضِبوا
(They found no fault with the Banū Umayya except that they are forbearing when angered.)
He means: they made the best of things appear ugly. The discussion of the position of «أَنْ» was also given in Sūrat al-Māʾida.
His saying: {أَن يُؤْمِنُواْ}: He used the future verb to alert that the torment was only because of their belief in the future; had they disbelieved in the future, they would not have been tormented for the belief of the past.

ukberi-tibyan:1-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالسَّمَاءِ ذَاتِ الْبُرُوجِ (١) وَالْيَوْمِ الْمَوْعُودِ (٢) وَشَاهِدٍ وَمَشْهُودٍ (٣) قُتِلَ أَصْحَابُ الْأُخْدُودِ (٤) النَّارِ ذَاتِ الْوَقُودِ (٥) إِذْ هُمْ عَلَيْهَا قُعُودٌ (٦)).
(وَ): the wāw is for the oath, and its answer is omitted, i.e. «لَتُبْعَثُنَّ» (you will surely be resurrected) and the like.
It is also said that its answer is «قُتِلَ», i.e. «لَقَدْ قُتِلَ» (indeed cursed are…).
It is also said that its answer is (إِنَّ بَطْشَ رَبِّكَ).
(وَالْيَوْمِ الْمَوْعُودِ): i.e. the [day] promised.
(النَّارِ) is a badal (substitute) for «الْأُخْدُود». It is also said that the implied form is «ذِي النَّارِ» (possessing the fire), because «الْأُخْدُود» is the trench in the ground. It has been read irregularly in the nominative (النَّارُ), i.e. «هُوَ النَّارُ» (it is the fire).
(إِذْ هُمْ) is an adverb (ẓarf) for «قُتِلَ». It is also said that the implied form is «اذْكُرْ» (remember).

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ فَتَنُوا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَتُوبُوا فَلَهُمْ عَذَابُ جَهَنَّمَ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابُ الْحَرِيقِ (١٠)).
(فَلَهُمْ عَذَابُ جَهَنَّمَ): it is said that it is like the words of the Exalted (فَإِنَّهُ مُلَاقِيكُمْ) [Translator's note: i.e. the fāʾ enters the khabar of «إِنَّ» because the relative noun resembles a condition.].

ukberi-tibyan:14-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الْوَدُودُ (١٤) ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ (١٥)).
The words of the Exalted (الْمَجِيدُ): in the nominative it is a naʿt (adjective) of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and in the genitive (الْمَجِيدِ) of «الْعَرْش».

ukberi-tibyan:17-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هَلْ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ الْجُنُودِ (١٧) فِرْعَوْنَ وَثَمُودَ (١٨)).
The words of the Exalted (فِرْعَوْنَ وَثَمُودَ): it is said that they are two badals (substitutes) for «الْجُنُود». It is also said that the implied form is «أَعْنِي» (I mean).

ukberi-tibyan:21-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (بَلْ هُوَ قُرْآنٌ مَجِيدٌ (٢١) فِي لَوْحٍ مَحْفُوظٍ (٢٢)).
The words of the Exalted (مَحْفُوظٍ): in the nominative (مَحْفُوظٌ) it is a naʿt (adjective) of the Mighty Qurʾān, and in the genitive (مَحْفُوظٍ) of «لَوْحٍ».

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Burūj
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿والسَّماءِ ذاتِ البُرُوجِ﴾: the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam) is: ﴿إنَّ بَطْشَ رَبِّكَ لَشَدِيدٌ﴾ [al-Burūj: 12]. It was said: ﴿ذاتِ البُرُوجِ﴾ means possessing the stars; and it was said: possessing the palaces, for palaces in heaven.

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿وَشاهِدٍ ومَشْهُودٍ﴾: «شاهِدٌ» (the witness) is Friday, and «وَمَشْهُودٌ» (the witnessed) is the Day of ʿArafa. It was also said: «وَشاهِدٌ» means the Prophet ﷺ, and «وَمَشْهُودٌ» is the Day of Resurrection, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿ذَلِكَ يَوْمٌ مَجْمُوعٌ لَهُ النّاسُ وذَلِكَ يَوْمٌ مَشْهُودٌ﴾ [Hūd: 103].

zajjaj:4-4.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قُتِلَ أصْحابُ الأُخْدُودِ﴾: «اَلْأُخْدُودُ» is a trench in the ground, and its plural is «أخادِيدُ». It was said: the People of the Trench were a people who worshipped an idol, and with them was a people who concealed their faith, worshipping Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and affirming His oneness. They came to know of them, so they dug a trench for them, filled it with fire and threw them into that fire; and they plunged into it and did not turn back from their religion, standing firm in Islam and certain that they were going to the Garden. It has come in the exegesis that the last of them to be thrown in was a woman with a nursing infant; when she saw the fire she turned her face away and shrank back, and the child said to her: "O mother, stand firm, and do not be a hypocrite." It was also said that he said to her: "It is nothing but a brief closing of the eyes." So she endured and was thrown into the fire. Whenever the Prophet ﷺ mentioned the People of the Trench, he sought refuge from the hardship of trial. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known the story of a people whose insight and true faith reached the point that they endured being burned with fire for the sake of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

zajjaj:8-8.t: ﴿وَما نَقَمُوا مِنهم إلا أنْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ العَزِيزِ الحَمِيدِ﴾, that is: they held no sin against them except their faith. Then He, Mighty and Majestic, made known what has been prepared for those who burned the believers, saying: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ فَتَنُوا المُؤْمِنِينَ والمُؤْمِناتِ﴾ [al-Burūj: 10], that is: they burned the believing men and the believing women. One says «فَتَنْتُ الشَّيْءَ», I burned it; and «اَلْفَتِينُ» is black stones, as though burned. ﴿فَلَهم عَذابُ جَهَنَّمَ ولَهم عَذابُ الحَرِيقِ﴾ [al-Burūj: 10]: the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: they will have the punishment of Hell for their unbelief, and they will have the punishment of burning for having burned the believing men and the believing women.

zajjaj:13-13.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنَّهُ هو يُبْدِئُ ويُعِيدُ﴾, that is: He originates creation, then restores it after its decay.

zajjaj:14-14.t: ﴿وَهُوَ الغَفُورُ الوَدُودُ﴾, that is: the one who loves His friends.

zajjaj:15-15.t: ﴿ذُو العَرْشِ المَجِيدُ﴾ — it is also read «اَلْمَجِيدِ». The meaning of «اَلْمَجِيدُ» is: the noble. Whoever put «اَلْمَجِيدِ» in the genitive made it an attribute of the Throne, and whoever put it in the nominative made it an attribute of «ذُو».

zajjaj:18-18.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فِرْعَوْنَ وثَمُودَ﴾: «فِرْعَوْنَ وثَمُودَ» are in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from «اَلْجُنُودِ»; the meaning is: "Has there come to you the story of Pharaoh and Thamūd?"

zajjaj:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿واللَّهُ مِن ورائِهِمْ مُحِيطٌ﴾, that is: none of them can escape Him; His power encompasses them.

zajjaj:21-21.t: ﴿بَلْ هو قُرْآنٌ مَجِيدٌ﴾ — it is also read «قُرْآنُ مَجِيدٍ». The reading is ﴿قُرْآنٌ مَجِيدٌ﴾, as a naʿt (adjective) of «قُرْآنٌ». Whoever read «قُرْآنُ» (in construct), the meaning is: "it is the Qur'an of a glorious Lord."

zajjaj:22-22.t: His saying: ﴿فِي لَوْحٍ مَحْفُوظٍ﴾: «اَلْقُرْآنُ» is in the Tablet, which is the Mother of the Book with Allah. It was also read «مَحْفُوظٌ», as an adjective of ﴿قُرْآنٌ﴾ [al-Burūj: 21]; the meaning is: "rather, it is a glorious Qur'an, preserved in a Tablet."
